ops._why: examples/12 per-tenant bulkhead on its library (S14); the slide is an excerpt

paragraphs: Resilience4j (the resilience4j-spring-boot4 starter) provides the bulkhead. Example 12 needs one limit per tenant, so instead of the @Bulkhead annotation, which names a single fixed instance, it asks the BulkheadRegistry for a bulkhead named after the tenant, created on first use from a shared 'tenant' configuration: five concurrent calls and a maximum wait of zero.

A tenant that fills its five permits gets BulkheadFullException and a 429 at once, while every other tenant keeps its own five. Refusing instead of queueing matters: a queue in front of a saturated tenant only turns its storm into a pile of waiting requests. At the platform layer, Istio's per-destination connection-pool limits complement these in-process limits.
